raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46293. When one streaming delta closes an invoke and also carries the next invoke's parameters, `MinimaxM2Detector.parse_streaming_increment` merges those parameters into the closing call. The client then receives, for example, `get_weather(Paris)` twice instead of `get_weather(Tokyo)` and `get_weather(Paris)`. Deltas this large happen when `TokenizerManager` coalesces queued outputs under load, with `--stream-interval > 1`, or with speculative decoding.

## Modifications

- `minimax_m2.py`: find `</invoke>` first, then pass only the text before it to `_parse_and_stream_parameters`. Before, the whole buffer was passed. The completion check reuses the same `end_pos`. Nothing else changes.
- New `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_minimax_m2_detector.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). This detector had no unit tests before. The three tests are:
  - both calls in one delta;
  - a delta that starts inside call 0 and ends inside call 1;
  - a no-argument call followed by a call with arguments.

## Accuracy Tests

The change is parser-only, so model outputs are unchanged.

- New tests: all 3 fail on `main` (052feb72a8) and pass with this change.
- `pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/`: the same 7 tests fail before and after this change (`test_deepseekv41_detector` grammar and `test_iquest_q1_detector` serving-path cases). They are unrelated to this PR, and my guess is the local xgrammar version. Nothing new fails.
- Differential fuzzing of `minimax-m2` compares streaming against `detect_and_parse`:
  - Chunkings: whole text, every 2-way split, random splits, and splits that never cut inside special tokens.
  - Cases: 12 (6 call shapes, each with and without leading text).
  - Before: 4 mismatching cases. After: 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The regex now runs over a shorter slice. This does not overlap with #42594, which changes how often the scan runs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (not needed).
- [ ] Accuracy and speed benchmarks (not applicable; parser-only).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Duplicate check

Open PRs that touch this detector are #28923, #35625, #36691, #42007, #42058 and #42594. I ran the reproduction on the #35625, #36691, #42007, #42058 and #42594 branches, and the bug is still there on all of them. #28923 changes only non-streaming `tool_index` ordinals. I found no existing issue for this symptom.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the differential fuzzer and to draft this change. I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the bug by hand, and ran the tests listed above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -316,14 +316,17 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
 
             # Parse parameters incrementally
             if self._function_name_sent:
-                # Process parameters and get any calls to emit
-                parameter_calls = self._parse_and_stream_parameters(self._buf, tools)
+                # Only parse parameters of the current invoke; the buffer may
+                # already hold the next invoke's parameters.
+                end_pos = self._buf.find(self.tool_call_function_end_token)
+                current_invoke = self._buf if end_pos == -1 else self._buf[:end_pos]
+                parameter_calls = self._parse_and_stream_parameters(
+                    current_invoke, tools
+                )
                 calls.extend(parameter_calls)
 
                 # Check if tool call is complete
-                if self.tool_call_function_end_token in self._buf:
-                    end_pos = self._buf.find(self.tool_call_function_end_token)
-
+                if end_pos != -1:
                     # Add closing brace to complete the JSON object
                     current_streamed = self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id]
                     if current_streamed:

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+import json
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
+from sglang.srt.function_call.minimax_m2 import MinimaxM2Detector
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _make_tools():
+    return [
+        Tool(
+            type="function",
+            function=Function(
+                name="get_weather",
+                parameters={
+                    "type": "object",
+                    "properties": {
+                        "city": {"type": "string"},
+                        "days": {"type": "integer"},
+                    },
+                },
+            ),
+        ),
+        Tool(
+            type="function",
+            function=Function(
+                name="get_time", parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}}
+            ),
+        ),
+    ]
+
+
+def _stream(chunks):
+    detector, tools = MinimaxM2Detector(), _make_tools()
+    names, args = {}, {}
+    for chunk in chunks:
+        for call in detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools).calls:
+            if call.name:
+                names[call.tool_index] = call.name
+            args[call.tool_index] = args.get(call.tool_index, "") + call.parameters
+    return [(names[i], json.loads(args[i] or "{}")) for i in sorted(names)]
+
+
+class TestMinimaxM2StreamingParameterScope(CustomTestCase):
+    """A delta that closes one invoke and carries the next invoke's
+    parameters must not leak those parameters into the closing call."""
+
+    TEXT = (
+        "<minimax:tool_call>\n"
+        '<invoke name="get_weather">\n'
+        '<parameter name="city">Tokyo</parameter>\n'
+        '<parameter name="days">3</parameter>\n'
+        "</invoke>\n"
+        '<invoke name="get_weather">\n'
+        '<parameter name="city">Paris</parameter>\n'
+        '<parameter name="days">1</parameter>\n'
+        "</invoke>\n"
+        "</minimax:tool_call>"
+    )
+
+    def test_two_calls_in_one_delta(self):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _stream([self.TEXT]),
+            [
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo", "days": 3}),
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris", "days": 1}),
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_delta_spanning_invoke_boundary(self):
+        split_at = self.TEXT.index('<parameter name="days">3')
+        end = self.TEXT.index("</invoke>", self.TEXT.index("Paris"))
+        chunks = [self.TEXT[:split_at], self.TEXT[split_at:end], self.TEXT[end:]]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _stream(chunks),
+            [
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo", "days": 3}),
+                ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris", "days": 1}),
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_no_arg_call_followed_by_call_with_args(self):
+        text = (
+            "<minimax:tool_call>\n"
+            '<invoke name="get_time">\n'
+            "</invoke>\n"
+            '<invoke name="get_weather">\n'
+            '<parameter name="city">Paris</parameter>\n'
+            "</invoke>\n"
+            "</minimax:tool_call>"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _stream([text]),
+            [("get_time", {}), ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"})],
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
